claims.summary: For a fixed nonzero finite-dimensional associative unital F2 algebra A of dimension r with fixed binary coordinates and unital left modules, these are equivalent: every simple A-module has F2 dimension1; all coordinates of ordered products of n arbitrary A inputs have polynomial-size fixed-depth AC0[2] circuits; every fixed-depth size-L F2 arithmetic formula has polynomial-size fixed-depth coordinate evaluation on A inputs. The positive side has a faithful upper triangular r-dimensional left regular representation, evaluator size O_A((L+r+2)^(r+4)+G), depth<=a+2h+3 for supplied entry circuits G,a. If a simple module is larger, finite-dimensional density gives a matrix-division-ring quotient with an odd-prime-order unit g: order3 binary block in matrix dimension>=2, or Cauchy in a nontrivial finite division-ring unit group of odd size. Any lift b yields rho(product((1-x_i)1+x_i b))=g^(sum x_i); fixed quotient/equality maps reduce MODp-zero to product coordinates. Smolensky1987 Theorem2 rules out polynomial-size fixed-depth parity circuits; no new Boolean lower bound. Under the full triangular-image hypotheses, positive-case A-valued old/placeholder schemes and same-probe two-image invariance have value circuits size O_A(E(S+r+1)^{O(r)}+G+U), depth<=a+u0+34, independent of original non-input proof structure. Prefix P^r vanishes via the faithful flag; initial-segment A_r need not be a certificate. No uniform growing-dimension, formal extraction, exact image-class closure, special-source impossibility in negative algebras, or Frege bound. Constants depend on fixed A; generic product length and formula encoding are distinct.
